Likely related people: @steipete and @openclaw-secops. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `fda6868e8efb5679bc9a94780881f283c4a36e6e` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | PR readiness rating was derived from proof quality, review findings, security review, and reviewer confidence. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Local read owner path: The final head checks regular-file identity before and after a nonblocking descriptor open, then reads that same handle.
Unicode and explicit-result behavior: Exact access is attempted first; variants are considered only after ENOENT/ENOTDIR, while empty, blank, and EOF outcomes are returned as visible text.
Sandbox MIME preservation: Sandbox MIME detection now consumes the already-read buffer through the existing full detector, preserving AVIF classification without a second bridge read. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Agent read tools turn local or sandboxed paths into bounded text or image results for the model. Sandbox filesystem guards validate the host descriptor before the bridge reads it, while the session read tool formats the resulting content and pagination guidance. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Agent read request] --> B[Exact path lookup] B --> C[Unicode fallback decision] C --> D[Local or sandbox descriptor guard] D --> E[Read buffer and MIME detection] E --> F[Text image or EOF result] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Does the sandbox owner approve the descriptor-opening change after reviewing the exact-head proof and completed checks? | **Approve after boundary proof:** Have the sandbox owner review the completed FIFO/descriptor proof and exact-head checks, then proceed with normal merge review. | Why: The changed sandbox filesystem boundary is CODEOWNERS-protected and changes the flags used before descriptor validation; source review found no vulnerability, but the ownership decision is human. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P2)** - The PR body links a pre-fix timeout but does not retain observable after-fix terminal or artifact output for the FIFO/read path. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - One exact-head baseline check is failing and the check set is incomplete, so merge readiness is not established. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - This bug fix adds about 95 net production lines; the local and sandbox guards have distinct owners, but the final review should confirm no duplicate safe-read policy remains. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - The protected sandbox boundary and missing after-fix evidence require human merge review rather than an automated repair.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Complete merge proof (recommended)** Attach redacted after-fix terminal or linked-action evidence for FIFO refusal and normal reads, finish exact-head checks, and obtain sandbox-owner approval. 2. **Accept source-only evidence** Maintainers may accept the current source and focused-test review despite the missing retained runtime artifact. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the single-buffer, descriptor-validated read flow with exact-first Unicode matching, then merge only after an after-fix FIFO trace, complete exact-head checks, and sandbox-owner approval. Maintainer dependency authorization for exact head ab5f5430e2337c117edfe4db82d38ceb5e1be8c5: approved. fs-safe 0.5.4 is authorized for the root dependency graph and bundled 1Password consumer. Prompt rejection of FIFOs and other special files is the intended compatibility and security behavior.

Maintainer policy confirmation for exact head ab5f5430e2337c117edfe4db82d38ceb5e1be8c5: default local agent reads must reject final symlinks. The supported target is a real regular file opened through the single fs-safe boundary; contained-symlink behavior is not part of this tool contract.

Agent/security owner approval for exact head ab5f5430e2337c117edfe4db82d38ceb5e1be8c5: approved. The default agent read contract intentionally rejects final symlinks, FIFOs, and other special files through the single fs-safe 0.5.4 boundary.
